verification_levels.primary: number read by us on the fetched original page on 2026-11-14; quote copied from it
verification_levels.derived: our arithmetic from primary-verified inputs (e.g. day counts between verified dates)
verification_levels.secondary: number from search extraction, press, or a third party; original not opened
verification_levels.unverified: not confirmed; do not display as fact

note: Web copy of docs/facts.json (unverified facts dropped). Alias keys used by the app point to the original ids (alias_of). Show the source link with every number.

water_people_served.label: Central Iowa Water Works' 12 member utilities serve more than 600,000 people in central Iowa.
water_people_served.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works Returns to Everyday Water Stewardship as Nitrate Removal Facility Concludes 193-Days of Operation
water_people_served.quote: Together, CIWW members serve more than 600,000 Iowans and distribute nearly 20 billion gallons of water each year.

plant_capacity_mgd.label: The Fleur Drive nitrate removal facility can treat up to 10 million gallons a day with 8 ion-exchange vessels: at least 3 and up to 7 run at once, with one kept for regeneration.
plant_capacity_mgd.source_title: What is the Nitrate Removal Facility?
plant_capacity_mgd.quote: The facility includes eight treatment vessels and can process up to 10 million gallons of water per day. When operating, at least three vessels run at a time, and up to seven can operate simultaneously

plant_days_2025.label: In 2025 the nitrate removal facility ran (partly or fully) on 112 days: 10-18 April and 28 April - 8 August 2025.
plant_days_2025.source_title: Iowa water quality: Central Iowa Water Works officials lift irrigation restrictions
plant_days_2025.quote: Central Iowa Water Works nitrate removal facility has operated for 112 days so far this year

plant_cost_2025_usd.label: Removing nitrate cost CIWW about $2.2 million in 2025: $1.6M operations & maintenance plus $0.6M capital.
plant_cost_2025_usd.source_title: What is the Nitrate Removal Facility?
plant_cost_2025_usd.quote: In 2025, the total annual cost was about $2.2 million, including $1.6 million in operations and maintenance and $600,000 in capital costs.

plant_om_cost_2025_usd.label: Operating and maintaining the nitrate removal facility cost about $1.6 million in 2025.
plant_om_cost_2025_usd.source_title: What is the Nitrate Removal Facility?
plant_om_cost_2025_usd.quote: In 2025, the total annual cost was about $2.2 million, including $1.6 million in operations and maintenance and $600,000 in capital costs.

plant_cost_per_day_usd.label: At full capacity (7 vessels) the facility costs about $16,000 a day to run; partial operation costs less.
plant_cost_per_day_usd.source_title: What is the Nitrate Removal Facility?
plant_cost_per_day_usd.quote: When operating at full capacity (seven vessels), the Nitrate Removal Facility costs approximately $16,000 per day to run.

plant_om_cost_2026_q1_usd.label: In the first quarter of 2026 the facility's O&M cost was about $660,000; CIWW says 2026 capital costs will be calculated in early 2027.
plant_om_cost_2026_q1_usd.source_title: What is the Nitrate Removal Facility?
plant_om_cost_2026_q1_usd.quote: In the first quarter of 2026, operations and maintenance costs were approximately $660,000. The 2026 capital costs will be calculated in early 2027.

plant_days_2026.label: In 2026 the nitrate removal facility ran a record 193 days: 6 Jan - 2 Mar and 9 Mar - 23 Jul 2026. The previous record was 177 days in 2015.
plant_days_2026.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works returns to everyday water stewardship as Nitrate Removal Facility concludes 193 days of operation
plant_days_2026.quote: The decision follows the conclusion of operations at the Nitrate Removal Facility, which ran for 193 days during the 2026 season before being taken offline on Thursday, July 23, 2026.

plant_days_record_prior.label: Before 2026, the longest nitrate removal run was 177 days, in 2015.
plant_days_record_prior.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works nitrate removal facility turns off, running for 112 days so far this year
plant_days_record_prior.quote: In 2015, the facility ran for 177 days

ban_2025_start.label: CIWW's first-ever lawn-watering ban (Stage III) began 12 June 2025 because nitrate in the Raccoon and Des Moines rivers was near record levels and nitrate removal was already at full capacity.
ban_2025_start.source_title: CIWW Resumes Commercial Irrigation, Continuing The Phased Exit From The Stage III Watering Ban
ban_2025_start.quote: commercial irrigation and lawn watering can resume on Wednesday, July 30, as part of the phased exit from the Stage III lawn watering ban initiated on June 12.

ban_2025_residential_eased.label: The 2025 ban was first eased for residential customers on 22 July 2025.
ban_2025_residential_eased.source_title: Lawn Watering To Resume July 22 Following A Phased Approach!
ban_2025_residential_eased.quote: On July 18, 2025, the Technical Committee voted to lift the ban on residential lawn watering beginning Tuesday, July 22 .

ban_2025_end.label: CIWW ended the Stage III lawn-watering ban on 7 Aug 2025 (moved to Stage I, voluntary 25% cut); all restrictions ended 15 Aug 2025.
ban_2025_end.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works ends lawn watering ban, moves to voluntary reduction stage
ban_2025_end.quote: Central Iowa Water Works has ended the Stage III lawn watering ban, it announced Thursday.

ban_2025_days.label: The mandatory 2025 Stage III lawn-watering ban lasted 56 days for all customers (12 Jun - 7 Aug 2025); homes were under the full ban for 40 days (to 22 Jul) and businesses for 48 days (to 30 Jul).
ban_2025_days.source_title: Derived from CIWW ban start/end releases

ban_2026_start.label: CIWW imposed its second mandatory lawn-watering ban on 8 June 2026, covering about 600,000 people.
ban_2026_start.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works Issues Stage 3 “Water Warning” Lawn Watering Ban Effective Immediately
ban_2026_start.quote: West Des Moines, Iowa (June 8, 2026) – The Central Iowa Water Works (CIWW) Board of Trustees has initiated Stage 3 of its Water Use Plan,implementing a mandatory lawn watering ban for residential, business, and government customers across the region.

ban_2026_residential_eased.label: Residential customers were moved off the 2026 lawn-watering ban (to Stage II, 50% voluntary cut) on 1 July 2026; the ban stayed for business and government customers until 20 July.
ban_2026_residential_eased.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works Eases Restrictions Through Phased Approach to Stage II
ban_2026_residential_eased.quote: The change is effective immediately for residential customers. The lawn watering ban will remain in effect for commercial and governmental customers

ban_2026_end.label: Residential customers left the 2026 lawn-watering ban on 1 July 2026; business and government customers on 20 July 2026. All restrictions ended 27 July 2026.
ban_2026_end.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works Transitions All Customers to Stage II Water Use Restrictions
ban_2026_end.quote: Effective July 20, 2026, residential, commercial, and governmental customers may resume outdoor irrigation while reducing lawn watering by approximately 50% and following the regional even/odd lawn watering schedule.

ban_2026_days.label: The 2026 mandatory lawn-watering ban lasted 23 days for homes (8 Jun - 1 Jul) and 42 days for business and government customers (8 Jun - 20 Jul 2026).

ban_lift_rule.label: To fully lift the 2025 ban, CIWW said at least one source must read 10 mg/L nitrate or less; it later kept the ban until both rivers showed a steady downward trend.
ban_lift_rule.quote: One of many factors to fully lift the ban requires that at least one water source – either the Raccoon River or Des Moines River – record nitrate concentrations at 10 mg/L or less.

raccoon_2025_peak_mgL.label: In 2025 the Raccoon River peaked at 20.55 mg/L nitrate-N on 8 June (only the second time above 20).
raccoon_2025_peak_mgL.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works shows how its Des Moines plant tests and treats drinking water with nitrates
raccoon_2025_peak_mgL.quote: On June 8, the Raccoon River hit 20.55 mg/L. A Central Iowa Water Works spokesperson said it marked the second time nitrate in the river surpassed 20 mg/L.

desmoines_2025_peak_mgL.label: In 2025 the Des Moines River peaked at about 17 mg/L nitrate-N on 12 June.
desmoines_2025_peak_mgL.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works shows how its Des Moines plant tests and treats drinking water with nitrates
desmoines_2025_peak_mgL.quote: On June 12, nitrate in the Des Moines River reached 17.15 mg/L — below the record 18.62 mg/L in 2013.

raccoon_record_mgL.label: The record Raccoon River nitrate level is 24.39 mg/L, set in 2013.
raccoon_record_mgL.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works shows how its Des Moines plant tests and treats drinking water with nitrates
raccoon_record_mgL.quote: The record was set in 2013 with 24.39 mg/L.

raccoon_2026_peak_mgL.label: In 2026 the USGS sensor on the Raccoon River at Van Meter recorded a maximum daily mean of 18.6 mg/L nitrate-N (28 May 2026); higher than the earlier-cited 17.45 mg/L (25 Jan).

raccoon_days_over10_2026_jun8.label: By 8 June 2026 the Raccoon River had been above 10 mg/L for 136 days that year, and the Des Moines River for 117 days.
raccoon_days_over10_2026_jun8.source_title: Why has CIWW implemented a lawn watering ban?
raccoon_days_over10_2026_jun8.quote: As of June 8, 2026, the Raccoon River has measured nitrate concentrations above 10 mg/L for 136 days, the Des Moines River has registered 117 days over 10mg/L

capital_state_grant_usd.label: Iowa lawmakers appropriated $25 million (2026) to expand CIWW's nitrate removal facility.
capital_state_grant_usd.source_title: KCCI Investigates: $1.2 billion in Central Iowa Water Works projects coming
capital_state_grant_usd.quote: For instance, expanding the nitrate removal facility got a $25 million appropriation from state lawmakers.

capital_nrf_expansion_cost_usd.label: Doubling the nitrate removal facility is estimated to cost about $40 million; ratepayers would cover what the $25M state grant does not.
capital_nrf_expansion_cost_usd.source_title: KCCI Investigates: $1.2 billion in Central Iowa Water Works projects coming
capital_nrf_expansion_cost_usd.quote: The estimated cost right now is $40 million. Ratepayers would make up the difference.

ag_share_river_nitrate_pct.label: A Polk County-commissioned, 2-year study by 16 scientists (CISWRA, July 2025) attributed roughly 70-80% of nitrate in the Raccoon and Des Moines rivers to agriculture (about 40% surplus fertilizer).
ag_share_river_nitrate_pct.source: Yahoo News / Iowa PBS Market to Market
ag_share_river_nitrate_pct.source_title: Polk County research report confirms nitrate in rivers directly tied to agriculture

isu_lbN_acre_yr.label: In an average year, an Iowa acre of corn or soybeans loses about 30 lb of nitrogen as nitrate to waterways.

kaspar_rye_pct.label: In a 14-year USDA-ARS tile-drainage experiment near Ames, a cereal rye cover crop cut nitrate load by 57% (concentration by 59%).
kaspar_rye_pct.source_title: Impact of broadcasting a cereal rye or oat cover crop before corn and soybean harvest on nitrate (Kaspar, Jaynes, Parkin, Moorman 2016, ASA-CSSA-SSSA abstract)
kaspar_rye_pct.quote: Over 14 years a cereal rye cover crop reduced nitrate concentrations by 59% and nitrate load by 57%.

kaspar_other_sites_pct.label: At other Iowa sites, Kaspar reports rye cover crops cut nitrate 15-48% (on-farm 2016: 40% lower load). Effects depend on rye growth, soil, weather and drainage timing.
kaspar_other_sites_pct.source_title: Winter Cover Crop Impacts on Erosion and Nitrate Losses in Tile Drainage (Kaspar SARE presentation)

inrs_cover_rye_pct.label: Iowa's Nutrient Reduction Strategy science assessment estimates a cereal rye cover crop cuts nitrate-N concentration in drainage by 31% on average (SD 29).
inrs_cover_rye_pct.source_title: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy (Feb 2025), Section 2: Iowa Science Assessment of Nonpoint Source Practices, Table 2

inrs_cover_rye_sd.label: Standard deviation of the INRS rye cover crop nitrate reduction: 29 percentage points (very variable).
inrs_cover_rye_sd.source_title: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy (Feb 2025), Section 2: Iowa Science Assessment of Nonpoint Source Practices, Table 2

inrs_cover_oat_pct.label: INRS: an oat cover crop cuts nitrate-N concentration about 28% (SD 2), based on a single study.
inrs_cover_oat_pct.source_title: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy (Feb 2025), Section 2: Iowa Science Assessment of Nonpoint Source Practices, Table 2
inrs_cover_oat_pct.quote: Oat 28 (2)** ‐5 (1) ... ** Based on 1 study with 3 years of corn and 2 years of soybean.

inrs_ext_rotation_pct.label: INRS: an extended rotation (at least 2 years of alfalfa in a 4-5 year rotation) cuts nitrate-N concentration by 42% on average (SD 12), with a +7% corn yield change.
inrs_ext_rotation_pct.source_title: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy (Feb 2025), Section 2: Iowa Science Assessment of Nonpoint Source Practices, Table 2
inrs_ext_rotation_pct.quote: At least 2 years of alfalfa in a 4 or 5 year Extended Rotations 42 (12) 7 (7) rotation

inrs_crp_pct.label: INRS: retiring row-crop land to CRP cuts nitrate-N concentration by 85% (SD 9); perennial energy crops by 72% (SD 23).
inrs_crp_pct.source_title: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy (Feb 2025), Section 2: Iowa Science Assessment of Nonpoint Source Practices, Table 2
inrs_crp_pct.quote: Land Retirement (CRP) ... 85 (9) ‐100 Compared to Spring‐ Applied Fertilizer

inrs_timing_pct.label: INRS: moving N application from fall to spring pre-plant cuts nitrate-N concentration about 6% (SD 25); a nitrification inhibitor (nitrapyrin) with fall N about 9% (SD 19).
inrs_timing_pct.source_title: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy (Feb 2025), Section 2: Iowa Science Assessment of Nonpoint Source Practices, Table 2
inrs_timing_pct.quote: Moving from Fall to Spring Pre‐plant Application 6 (25) 4 (16)

inrs_mrtn_pct.label: INRS: reducing N rate to the MRTN (133 lb N/ac corn after soybean; 190 lb N/ac continuous corn) cuts nitrate-N about 10% statewide, with about -1% corn yield.
inrs_mrtn_pct.source_title: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy (Feb 2025), Section 2: Iowa Science Assessment of Nonpoint Source Practices, Table 2
inrs_mrtn_pct.quote: Reduce to Maximum Return to Nitrogen value 149 kg N/ha (133 lb N/ac) for CS and 213 kg 10‡ ‐1‡‡ ... ‡ Reduction calculated based on initial application rate for each Major Land Resource Area (MLRA).

inrs_bioreactor_pct.label: INRS: woodchip bioreactors cut nitrate-N about 43% (SD 21) in the drainage water they treat.
inrs_bioreactor_pct.source_title: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy (Feb 2025), Section 2: Iowa Science Assessment of Nonpoint Source Practices, Table 2

inrs_sat_buffer_pct.label: INRS: saturated buffers cut nitrate-N about 50% (SD 13) in the drainage they treat.
inrs_sat_buffer_pct.source_title: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy (Feb 2025), Section 2: Iowa Science Assessment of Nonpoint Source Practices, Table 2
inrs_sat_buffer_pct.quote: Additional P removal of about ½ pound of P Saturated Buffer 50 (13) per year

inrs_wetland_pct.label: INRS: nitrate-removal wetlands cut nitrate-N about 52% (one report, no SD) in the water they treat.
inrs_wetland_pct.source_title: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy (Feb 2025), Section 2: Iowa Science Assessment of Nonpoint Source Practices, Table 2
inrs_wetland_pct.quote: Wetlands Targeted Water Quality 52† ... † Based on one report looking at multiple wetlands in Iowa (Helmers et al., 2008a).

iowa_cover_acres.label: Iowa farmers planted about 3.87 million acres of cover crops in 2024, about 16.7% of corn and soybean acres.
iowa_cover_acres.source_title: Farmers expanding cover crop, no-till acres across the state (INREC Nutrient Reduction Survey)

iowa_cover_share_pct.label: Cover crops are on about 16.7% of Iowa corn and soybean acres (2024).
iowa_cover_share_pct.source_title: Farmers expanding cover crop, no-till acres across the state

idals_costshare_usd_ac.label: Iowa's state cover crop cost-share (2026 sign-up) pays $30/acre for first-time users and $20/acre for returning users, up to 160 acres.
idals_costshare_usd_ac.source: Iowa Dept. of Agriculture and Land Stewardship
idals_costshare_usd_ac.source_title: Secretary Naig Opens Sign-Up for Annual Cover Crop Cost-Share Program
idals_costshare_usd_ac.quote: Farmers planting cover crops for the first time are eligible for $30 per acre. Farmers who have previously planted cover crops are eligible for $20 per acre.

gdmw_costshare_usd_ac.label: In the 22-county Greater Des Moines Watershed (launched 22 Jun 2026), cover crop cost-share is $25/acre on up to 500 acres, stackable with the state program (up to 660 acres).
gdmw_costshare_usd_ac.source: Iowa Dept. of Agriculture and Land Stewardship
gdmw_costshare_usd_ac.source_title: Secretary Naig Launches Greater Des Moines Watershed Program, Announces Enhanced Cover Crop Cost-Share in 22 Counties
gdmw_costshare_usd_ac.quote: increasing cost-share payments for both new and existing cover crop users to $25 per acre and increasing the maximum eligible acreage to 500 acres per farmer or landowner.

crop_insurance_discount_usd_ac.label: Iowa's cover crop crop-insurance discount takes $5/acre off premiums for acres not funded by other cover crop programs.
crop_insurance_discount_usd_ac.source: Iowa Dept. of Agriculture and Land Stewardship
crop_insurance_discount_usd_ac.source_title: Secretary Naig Opens Sign-Up Window for Iowa's Crop Insurance Discount Program
crop_insurance_discount_usd_ac.quote: The innovative program offers farmers a $5 per acre premium reduction for fall-planted cover crops.

eqip_340_usd_ac.label: NRCS EQIP pays about $74/acre in Iowa (FY2026, regular rate) for a single-species cover crop (practice 340); about $89/acre for historically underserved producers.
eqip_340_usd_ac.source_title: EQIP and CSP After the 2025 Budget Law: What Changed and How to Apply

rye_seeding_cost_usd_ac.label: Custom drilling of cover crop seed in Iowa averaged $19.05/acre in 2026 (range $9-25); aerial seeding $14.70/acre (range $10-18).
rye_seeding_cost_usd_ac.source_title: 2026 Iowa Farm Custom Rate Survey (Ag Decision Maker A3-10)
rye_seeding_cost_usd_ac.quote: Aerial seeding of cover crop / acre 14.70 15.00 10.00 - 18.00 25 Drilling cover crop seed / acre 19.05 19.25 9.00 - 25.00 39

rye_seed_cost_usd_ac.label: ISU Extension estimates the added cost of cereal rye seed at about $25 per acre (in an organic no-till budget); seeding adds about $15-19/acre.
rye_seed_cost_usd_ac.source_title: Organic No-Till Grain Production with Cover Crops (Ag Decision Maker A1-92)
rye_seed_cost_usd_ac.quote: Added seed costs for the cereal rye are about $25 per acre.

fert_price_usd_lbN.label: Iowa anhydrous ammonia averaged $1,096/ton in May 2026 (USDA AMS), which is about $0.67 per lb of N.

mcl_mgL.label: The EPA drinking-water limit (MCL) for nitrate is 10 mg/L measured as nitrogen, set to protect infants under six months from blue baby syndrome (methemoglobinemia).
mcl_mgL.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works shows how its Des Moines plant tests and treats drinking water with nitrates
mcl_mgL.quote: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) set the legal limit of nitrate in public drinking water at 10 mg/L to protect against “blue baby syndrome,” a potentially fatal condition for infants.

health_cancer_iwhs.label: Iowa Women's Health Study analyses (NCI) found higher thyroid, ovarian, bladder and kidney cancer risk with higher long-term public-water nitrate, but no link to colorectal or pancreatic cancer in that cohort.
health_cancer_iwhs.source_title: Water contaminants and cancer risk: arsenic, disinfection byproducts, and nitrate
health_cancer_iwhs.quote: women with higher average nitrate levels in public water supplies had increased risks of thyroid, ovarian, bladder, and kidney cancers

usgs_vanmeter_da_sqmi.label: The Raccoon River at Van Meter gauge (USGS 05484500) drains 3,441 square miles.
usgs_vanmeter_da_sqmi.quote: 05484500 Raccoon River at Van Meter, IA ... drain_area_va 3441 ... huc_cd 07100006

usgs_2ndave_da_sqmi.label: The Des Moines River at 2nd Ave gauge (USGS 05482000) drains 6,245 square miles.
usgs_2ndave_da_sqmi.quote: 05482000 Des Moines River at 2nd Avenue at Des Moines, IA ... drain_area_va 6245 ... huc_cd 07100004

usgs_pcode_99133.label: USGS parameter 99133 = nitrate plus nitrite, water, in situ, mg/L as nitrogen (continuous sensor).
usgs_pcode_99133.quote: 99133 Nitrate plus nitrite, water, in situ, milligrams per liter as nitrogen

nasa_nfews_prior_art.label: NASA is funding a 3-year University of Iowa project, with Des Moines Water Works, Cedar Rapids and Iowa City, to forecast nitrate days ahead from NASA satellite data plus Iowa water-quality sensors (announced July 2026).
nasa_nfews_prior_art.source_title: NASA funds new nitrate forecasting tool for Iowa water supply
nasa_nfews_prior_art.quote: NASA is funding the project for three years.

inrs_nonpoint_share_pct.label: Iowa's Nutrient Reduction Strategy says nonpoint sources (mostly farmland) account for 92% of the nitrogen entering Iowa streams each year; point sources (cities, industry) about 7-8%.
inrs_nonpoint_share_pct.source_title: Iowa Nutrient Reduction Strategy (Feb 2025), Executive Summary and Section 1: Policy
inrs_nonpoint_share_pct.quote: Nonpoint sources account for 92% of the TN and 80% of the TP entering Iowa streams annually.

inrs_rye_corn_yield_pct.label: INRS lists a -6% (SD 7) corn yield change after a rye cover crop; the 2024 Science Team update revised it to 0% (SD 10). INRS does not count soybean yield effects.
inrs_rye_corn_yield_pct.source_title: INRS Section 2 Table 2 (Feb 2025) and INRS Nitrogen BMP Efficiencies update (Mar 2024)

rye_before_soybean_yield.unit: of 28 location-years with no yield reduction
rye_before_soybean_yield.label: In 28 location-years of Midwest trials (2019-2021), terminating a cereal rye cover crop before, at or after soybean planting did not reduce soybean yield in 27 of 28 cases; there was also no significant yield gain.
rye_before_soybean_yield.source_title: Cereal rye cover crop termination at or before soybean planting has minimal effect on soybean yield across the midwestern US (Severo Silva et al. 2024, Field Crops Research 312:109393)
rye_before_soybean_yield.quote: Results showed that termination timing did not reduce soybean yield in 27 of 28 location-years compared to no cover crop treatment.

extended_rotation_marsden.label: In a 2003-2011 Iowa field trial (ISU Marsden Farm), 3- and 4-year rotations run with less synthetic N fertilizer and herbicide had grain yields and profit similar to or greater than the conventional corn-soybean rotation.
extended_rotation_marsden.source_title: Increasing cropping system diversity balances productivity, profitability and environmental health (Davis, Hill, Chase, Johanns, Liebman 2012, PLoS ONE 7(10):e47149)
extended_rotation_marsden.quote: Grain yields, mass of harvested products, and profit in the more diverse systems were similar to, or greater than, those in the conventional system, despite reductions of agrichemical inputs.

prairie_strips_nitrate.label: Converting about 10% of a cropped watershed to prairie strips cut nitrate concentration in shallow groundwater by about 72% and total N in surface runoff by about 70% (ISU STRIPS, Schulte et al. 2017 PNAS).
prairie_strips_nitrate.source_title: Prairie strips improve biodiversity and the delivery of multiple ecosystem services from corn-soybean croplands (Schulte et al. 2017, PNAS); ISU news release 2017-10-03

stage3_trigger_demand_pct.label: CIWW considers a Stage III lawn-watering ban when customer demand exceeds 90% of treatment-plant capacity; in June 2026 demand crossed that threshold and was projected to hit 98%.
stage3_trigger_demand_pct.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works issues lawn watering ban due to high nitrates levels
stage3_trigger_demand_pct.quote: The third stage is considered when customer demand exceeds 90% of the capacity of the treatment plants, said Amy Kahler, CEO of Des Moines Water Works

lawn_watering_share_pct.label: Lawn watering can account for up to 40% of regional summer water demand in the CIWW system.
lawn_watering_share_pct.source_title: Why has CIWW implemented a lawn watering ban?
lawn_watering_share_pct.quote: Lawn watering is the single largest discretionary use of water during the summer and can account for up to 40% of regional water demand.

nrf_vs_demand.label: The 10 million gallon/day nitrate removal facility is a fraction of normal demand at the Des Moines plants, which can be 70-80 million gallons/day; treated water is blended.
nrf_vs_demand.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works shows how its Des Moines plant tests and treats drinking water with nitrates
nrf_vs_demand.quote: While highly effective, the nitrate removal facility has capacity for 10 million gallons a day. Morarend explained that’s a fraction of normal demand, which can be 70-80 million gallons.

restrictions_2025_start.label: 2025 water restrictions began 30 May 2025 with a voluntary 25% cut, a 50% request on 11 June, and the mandatory ban on 12 June; all restrictions ended 15 August 2025.
restrictions_2025_start.source_title: Iowa water quality: Central Iowa Water Works officials lift irrigation restrictions
restrictions_2025_start.quote: voted unanimously to resume normal irrigation and lawn watering practices for the first time since May 30, 2025

strips_cost_usd_treated_ac.unit: USD per treated crop acre per year
strips_cost_usd_treated_ac.label: ISU STRIPS estimates prairie strips cost about $26-33 per treated crop acre per year (one acre of prairie treats about nine acres of crop), before CRP payments; most of the cost is land rent / foregone revenue.

strips_crp_cost_reduction_pct.label: Under a 15-year continuous CRP contract (CP-43: 55% cost share, 90% annual rent, signing bonus 32.5% of rent), ISU STRIPS estimates the cost of prairie strips falls by about 75%, to about $7-8 per treated crop acre per year.

range.unit: USD per treated crop acre per year after CRP

strips_crp_cost_reduction_pct.quote: approximately 75% reduction, thus costing about $8 per year per crop acre treated with prairie

tile_delivery_mcisaac_hu.unit: % of NNI exported by rivers (non-tiled region)
tile_delivery_mcisaac_hu.label: In tile-drained central Illinois, riverine nitrate-N export equalled net N inputs (NNI); in non-tiled southern Illinois it was 25-37% of NNI (McIsaac & Hu 2004, cited in David, Drinkwater & McIsaac 2010, J. Environ. Qual. 39:1657-1667).
tile_delivery_mcisaac_hu.source_title: Sources of Nitrate Yields in the Mississippi River Basin (David, Drinkwater, McIsaac 2010, JEQ 39(5):1657-1667)
tile_delivery_mcisaac_hu.quote: In the tile-drained region (central Illinois) NNI was equal to riverine nitrate N export, whereas in the non-tiled region (southern Illinois) riverine export was between 25 and 37% of NNI.

people_served.label: Central Iowa Water Works' 12 member utilities serve more than 600,000 people in central Iowa.
people_served.source_title: Central Iowa Water Works Returns to Everyday Water Stewardship as Nitrate Removal Facility Concludes 193-Days of Operation
people_served.quote: Together, CIWW members serve more than 600,000 Iowans and distribute nearly 20 billion gallons of water each year.

ban_days_2025.label: The mandatory 2025 Stage III lawn-watering ban lasted 56 days for all customers (12 Jun - 7 Aug 2025); homes were under the full ban for 40 days (to 22 Jul) and businesses for 48 days (to 30 Jul).
ban_days_2025.source_title: Derived from CIWW ban start/end releases

ban_days_2026.label: The 2026 mandatory lawn-watering ban lasted 23 days for homes (8 Jun - 1 Jul) and 42 days for business and government customers (8 Jun - 20 Jul 2026).

fert_price_usd_lb_N.label: Iowa anhydrous ammonia averaged $1,096/ton in May 2026 (USDA AMS), which is about $0.67 per lb of N.
